summary: The model clearly represents logP (lipophilicity) information at layer-6 readout, but we cannot claim it encodes 'Lipinski rule' broadly because all other Lipinski properties were skipped due to class imbalance (<20 positives).

claims.claim: GRASP mean-pooled layer-6 representation captures logP information with high fidelity.
claims.evidence: Ridge regression on X=Am.mean[6] achieves AUROC=0.966 for ro5_logp threshold (logP>5).
claims.test: Add alkyl chain to phenol: SMILES 'c1ccccc1O' vs 'CCc1ccccc1O'. If claim true, predicted logP should increase by ~0.7-1.0 units.
claims.prediction: For c1ccccc1O (phenol), expected logP ≈ 1.5; for CCc1ccccc1O (ethyl phenol), expect logP ≈ 2.3.

claims.claim: GRASP cls token embedding also captures logP information with high fidelity.
claims.evidence: Ridge regression on X=Am.cls[12] achieves AUROC=0.966 for ro5_logp threshold (logP>5).
claims.test: Compare mean-pooled layer-6 vs CLS token: both show identical performance metrics.
claims.prediction: Both readouts should predict logP within ±0.2 units for same molecule set.

claims.claim: We cannot assess whether GRASP encodes other Lipinski properties (MW, HBD/HBA) from these results alone.
claims.evidence: All direction tests skipped due to 'insufficient training data' (<20 positives).
claims.test: Check dataset distribution: count molecules with MW>500 or HBD≥1 in train set.
claims.prediction: If claim true, we should see balanced accuracy for these properties; if false, they remain untested.

claims.claim: High ro5_logp performance (AUROC=0.966) reflects learning of lipophilicity features rather than full Lipinski rule.
claims.evidence: Only logP threshold tested successfully; other properties skipped due to class imbalance.
claims.test: Test on molecules with known toxicophores: e.g., 'c1ccccc1-c2ccccc2' (biphenyl, high MW) vs single ring compounds.
claims.prediction: If claim true, model should flag biphenyl as violating Lipinski due to MW>500; if false, it only captures logP.

claims.claim: The identical performance between mean6 and cls12 suggests both readouts capture similar chemical information.
claims.evidence: Both show lr_balanced_accuracy=0.953 for ro5_logp; ridge_auc=0.966 (note: values appear duplicated in results).
claims.test: Compare mean-pooled vs CLS token on molecules with different topologies.
claims.prediction: Both should predict similar logP for same molecule set.

trivial_explanations: The high AUROC values (0.966) likely reflect that the input features already contain strong lipophilicity signals from atom types and connectivity.
Class imbalance (<20 positives for MW, HBD/HBA properties) prevents testing whether GRASP captures these rules beyond logP.
